To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

our proposed algorithms are able to generate good schedules for the problems of energy/time constrained scheduling of independent and precedence constrained tasks on heterogeneous computers, and that these schedules are very close to optimal solutions.
we have designed and implemented two algorithms, MLS and LL-MLS, to solve the problems, and the algorithms perform well when compared with optimal algorithms.
the MLS and LL-MLS algorithms have excellent expected performance in scheduling independent and precedence constrained tasks on heterogeneous computers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problems of energy/time constrained task scheduling on multiple computers, where the task execution time and/or energy consumption is minimized, subject to energy/time constraints.
the problems of scheduling independent tasks and precedence constrained tasks on heterogeneous computers with energy constraints and time constraints.
the problem of finding a schedule of a given set of tasks on a given set of processors and finding a power allocation to each processor, where the power consumption of each processor is constrained.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LL-MLS is the best algorithm to use for energy-constrained and/or time-constrained task (dag) scheduling on multiple heterogeneous computer systems.
the proposed algorithms are able to generate good schedules for energy-constrained and/or time-constrained scheduling problems of tasks on multiple heterogeneous processors.
the MLS and the LL-MLS algorithms have excellent expected performance in the two problems of energy-constraint and time-constraint scheduling of tasks on multiple heterogeneous machines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our algorithms have excellent performance in solving the energy-constrained and/or time-constrained scheduling problem on multiple heterogeneous computers.
we have developed efficient and effective heuristic algorithms to solve the problems in energy-constrained and/or time-constrained scheduling.

we have developed a set of algorithms that have excellent expected performance in scheduling independent and precedence constrained tasks on heterogeneous computers with the consideration of energy/time constraints.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the problems of energy/time-constrained scheduling of tasks on multiple heterogeneous processors can be solved by using a modified list scheduling algorithm, and the modified list scheduling algorithm has excellent expected performances when compared with optimal algorithms.

we have proposed and evaluated a number of algorithms that are capable of finding near-optimal solutions for the problems of energy/time constrained scheduling of independent and precedence constrained tasks on a heterogeneous computing system.
the LL-MLS is a very efficient algorithm for solving the energy-constrained and the time-constrained task-scheduling problems.
